AI has had an impact on jobs for ten years. Google Maps, appointment schedulers, voice recognition, translation, adaptive design, self-driving cars... Jesus, how much more obvious does it have to get?
Self driving robotic trucks will make a big impact, even if just driving from Distro center to Distro center.

As much as I would love to see a general rollout of self driving vehicles - talk to some people in the industry. It will be a long while before the algorithms are solid enough to be a full replacement for the human driver. At best it could be a really good cruise control now and for at least the next few years.

In test tracks and in advertising campaigns you might have short runs of AI trucking - but the general rollout would have to be absolutely rock solid. It simply is not there. There are still far too many points of failure and far too many places where the AI does not come up with the correct solution for it to be something to trust to drive a 50 thousand pound load.

The test cases that are publicized now are in best case environments without a lot of extraneous details that fall outside the training sets. They are also reliant on a lot of very finicky tech that fails frequently in ways that cannot be predicted. Its sort of like were VR was about 30 years ago. The idea was there - and a lot of the tech was there - and you could build an expensive test rig for it - but it was not public ready.

It may not be 50 years - but I think it would be optimistic to think there would be general purpose trucking done by AI in 20 years.

Some problems are really hard. This problem is really really hard.

The fact that a full load-refuel-unload solution including paperwork and whatever needs to be done on the road probably won't be available for a long time doesn't mean that self-driving vehicles aren't affecting the job market. Just a truck that can do highway driving could change teams to single-person routes. Not to mention taxis, mines, and very short range material movement in factories.

He is not wrong. You are not going to get good general purpose AI for things like self driving trucks for many years. It will be in the gimmick stage - like VR for the past 20 years - for at least another decade. Its not going to be allowed to broadly be rolled out until it is rock solid.

And people really don't understand that machine learning at this point has to be trained very specifically on the types of tasks that it will need to perform. It does not deal well with things outside its training set. Even DeepMind - that is the first really generalizable learning machine - does not generalize well.

Machine learning algorithms often optimize on things that humans would never pick up on - that are quirky details in the training set. When you pull them out of the training set - the system has to relearn how to do tasks from scratch. They do not deal well with ambiguity and even really good stuff needs heavily coded information to be successful.

For a very long time it will be augmenting human ability - not replacing it.

That does not mean that kiosks and a screen will not take over for fast food restaurants. But it does mean that there will not be a robot waiter past the gimmick point for a long time.

I have been an engineer using machine learning for many years and though it is getting better at a fast pace - what would be needed to really replace humans is well outside the capacity for any intelligent system.

I think the tech journalists and futurists would like to see AI now - but I have my doubts as to whether we will even get there once we have the processing power of a human mind in a box. I think the algorithms honed by a billion years of evolution are not easily replicated.
OTOH I expect technology to progress faster than many expect.

If Moores law can continue - and we are right up against the edge on that - and if the algorithms can be found - maybe. But the space explored is vast and not something that can be built in by humans. It requires training in millions of situations and efficient optimization on the correct ones for environments that are unpredictable. Humans are really good at this but only because we have a crazy level of parallel threads running these algorithms and each of us writes our own version.

AI does not have the culling mechanisms we have for bad paths and does not have the metadata overlay we have about the nature of the world. In a lot of cases its really just lidar creating a point cloud attached to GPS. Its not at the point where it knows enough about what is going on around it to be a functional replacement.

I envision truckers getting really good cruise control and maybe some collision avoidance assistance - but I would be really surprised if there is a single line of self driving fleet vehicles in 10 years.

I want it to be true. I REALLY wanted AGI to be real before my program ends.
